answer: Data-shard custody enforces sybil resistance by requiring agents to hold unique assets; an honest agent incurs a 1 unit cost, while 1,000 fakes incur a 1,000,000 unit penalty. The verifier requests random files from a stored grove to confirm identity. If an agent fails a retrieve-on-dawn proof, the shard is forfeited. This nebula of stored state prevents identity duplication, as the scarce cost per unit remains constant.
